$about: The 49-event contract of docs/02b-integration-map.md, made mechanical.
CLAUDE.md describes app/lib/events/** as 'the 49-event contract, generated
from contracts/events/' and states that 'an event outside the canonical 49
is a bug, not a feature'. NEITHER DIRECTORY EXISTED. The contract lived only
as prose in a 57 KB markdown table, which means the rule was documentation
and the constitution's own test — a type that does not compile, a build that
goes red — was not met by it.
This file is the source. scripts/generate-events.ts turns it into
app/lib/events/catalog.generated.ts and scripts/events-contract.test.ts
makes drift a red build in both directions.
WHY THE GHOSTS MATTER AS MUCH AS THE CATALOG. §2 of 02b calls them 'the real
finding': 262 declared events reconciled to 40, and every collision was a
silent integration failure that would have shipped. A module waiting for
`opportunity.closed_won` never fires on a sale, and nothing anywhere goes
red — the sale simply is not celebrated, tasks are not closed, and reporting
is short one row. A positive registry cannot catch that: the ghost name never
appears in the catalog, so a checker that only validates catalog membership
sees a name it does not know rather than a name that was RULED OUT and knows
the difference matters. The ghosts carry their remap target and their
consequence so the failure names itself.
TWO PLACES WHERE THIS FILE DEPARTS FROM THE DOCUMENT, both deliberate:
1. MONEY. §4's payloads name money fields with a `_usd` suffix —
`deal_value_annual_premium_usd`, `delta_usd`, `amount_usd`. That suffix
invites a JS number, which CLAUDE.md makes a build error outside
app/lib/money/**. Every one of them is typed `money` here and generates as
the branded Money type, crossing JSON as a string of whole cents. The
suffix is dropped from the field name so the wire shape cannot be read as
dollars. This is a naming change, not a semantic one.
2. THE ENVELOPE IS NOT REPEATED IN PAYLOADS. §4's first row spells the nine
envelope fields into lead.created's payload and then writes 'ENVELOPE, …'
for the rest. Repeating them per event is how two definitions drift, so
the envelope is declared once, here, and composed by the generator.
PAYLOAD PROVENANCE IS MARKED, because the two halves of the catalog were not
specified to the same depth. The 40 of §4 carry a ratified field list. The 9
of §4b Amendment 1 carry an emitter, a trigger and a rationale but NO payload
table — so their fields here are derived from those three sentences and are
flagged `"payload": "derived"`. A derived payload is a proposal that compiles,
not a ratified contract, and the module that first emits one should be the
thing that settles it.

envelope.$note: §3. Not one of the 262 originally-declared events carried one. Default-deny scoping: every consumer filters by tenant_id and, unless it is the leaderboard projection, by owner_user_id.

events.name: lead.created
events.note: Starts the speed-to-lead clock; received_at_utc_ms is millisecond precision because the measurement runs from here. NEVER emit without owner_user_id — in a silo model an unowned lead is invisible to everyone.

events.name: lead.duplicate_detected
events.note: Silo rule: the payload may name matched_owner_user_id, but no consumer may render the other seller's lead detail to the incoming path.

events.name: lead.import_completed
events.note: Import is the second dedupe checkpoint, not a bypass of the first.

events.name: contact.created
events.note: Deliberately low-consumption. NOT an automation trigger — the plain-English vocabulary uses 'lead created'. Keeping both prevents Intake and Contacts from double-emitting the same business fact.

events.name: contact.merged
events.note: The cross-silo landmine: a merge can move a closed-won deal between sellers and therefore move money on a public leaderboard. Consent resolution takes the most restrictive value — an opt-out on either record wins.

events.name: contact.became_client
events.note: Consumed from opportunity.won on the contact's FIRST win. This is what turns a one-shot FE sale into a second opportunity on the same contact.

events.name: consent.updated
events.note: ONE canonical consent event. Aloware enforces DNC/STOP on its side; we mirror it so our UI never offers a button that will be refused, and so we can prove state at any point in time.

events.name: opportunity.created
events.note: Intake-born opportunities are announced by lead.created, which carries opportunity_id — this one is cross-sell, recycle or manual.

events.name: opportunity.stage_changed
events.note: Must carry to_stage_is_closed/closed_type RESOLVED AT MOVE TIME — stage config is per-seller mutable, so a consumer re-reading config later can reach a different answer than the moment of the move. Earnings deliberately does NOT consume this; it consumes opportunity.won only.

events.name: opportunity.won
events.note: THE money event. deal_value_annual_premium is non-null and enforced by the win gate, which is what guarantees Earnings math is never blank.

events.name: opportunity.lost
events.note: Loss reasons are tenant-configurable but the code list must stay stable; Reporting keys on loss_reason_code, never the label.

events.name: opportunity.value_changed
events.note: The single most-forgotten link in the money chain. If Earnings only listens to opportunity.won, editing a premium after close silently corrupts a PUBLIC all-time leaderboard.

events.name: opportunity.reopened
events.note: Non-negotiable for an ALL-TIME board: with no monthly reset, an un-reversed bad win is wrong forever. This is why earnings is an append-only delta ledger, not a mutable total.

events.name: opportunity.went_cold
events.note: ONE event, not four — 'stale', 'rotting', 'idle', 'dormant' all collapse here. Fires once per crossing (idempotent per opportunity per cold episode) or it becomes notification spam. R1.7: one threshold, cold_threshold_days, default 7. Board rot styling is derived from last_activity_at, not from a second event.

events.name: opportunity.recycled
events.note: Recycling aged leads is a TCPA landmine: consent gathered 14 months ago may no longer be defensible. consent_age_days must ride the event so Communications can refuse.

events.name: call.initiated
events.note: Emitted by us before Aloware confirms; reconciled by call.completed on aloware_call_id. Carrying consent + local time on the dial event is what makes TCPA provable per call rather than per contact.

events.name: call.completed
events.note: Idempotent on aloware_call_id — webhooks retry and arrive out of order. 'Missed call' in the automation vocabulary is this event filtered to direction=inbound + disposition_canonical=missed; it is NOT a separate event.

events.name: call.enriched
events.note: Three Aloware webhooks (recording / transcript / summary) collapse into ONE internal event with parts_available[] so consumers need one handler, not three. Updates the EXISTING timeline entry in place — never a duplicate row.

events.name: message.sent
events.note: Channel-agnostic by design — the whatsapp_reserved slot is how WhatsApp arrives later without a new event family. Appointment reminders ARE messages: there is no separate appointment.reminder_sent event, it is this with related_appointment_id.

events.name: message.received
events.note: AUTO-PAUSES every active sequence — the reply rule. A lead replying while a robot keeps texting is the fastest way to lose trust and invite a TCPA complaint, so this must reach Automations before the next sequence step is due. intent_hint=stop drives consent.updated.

events.name: message.delivery_failed
events.note: Bad-contact-data rate per vendor_id is a purchasing lever for the owner, not just a technical error log.

events.name: appointment.scheduled
events.note: starts_at_utc + contact_timezone are both mandatory: reminders fired in the wrong local time are both useless and a TCPA hours risk. Booking also auto-pauses nurture sequences — booked means stop selling the meeting.

events.name: appointment.rescheduled
events.note: originating_no_show_id is what lets Reporting prove the no-show recovery flow actually recovers revenue.

events.name: appointment.canceled
events.note: US spelling with one L, matching the catalog. The ghost `meeting.cancelled` is the two-L British form and is registered as such.

events.name: appointment.completed
events.note: linked_call_id is what ties an Aloware phone appointment to its recording and AI summary in one timeline entry.

events.name: appointment.no_showed
events.note: Plain-English named on purpose, not a generic appointment.status_changed — the automation vocabulary must read like a sentence a seller would say.

events.name: calendar.sync_failed
events.note: Silent calendar drift is how a seller misses a meeting and blames the CRM. Self-service reconnection is the point. Google Calendar sync itself is deferred to V1.1 — this event exists so the deferral does not have to be undone by adding a name later.

events.name: activity.created
events.note: source_event_name is what lets a seller ask 'why is this on my list today' and get a real answer. A single Activity object is what makes My Day possible.

events.name: activity.completed
events.note: Auto-completion from call/SMS events is the whole point: the seller never does bookkeeping, and the cold-lead rule stays honest because last_activity_at is real.

events.name: activity.overdue
events.note: Idempotent per activity per escalation_level, or it becomes the notification firehose that trains sellers to ignore the app.

events.name: sequence.enrolled
events.note: Enrollment state is OURS even when Aloware executes. Two engines with two states is how a replied lead keeps getting texted.

events.name: sequence.paused
events.note: ONE pause event with a reason, not four differently-named ones. pause_reason=consent_revoked has legal weight and must stay distinguishable from a friendly reply-pause forever. Communications MUST call Aloware disenroll or Aloware keeps sending.

events.name: sequence.completed
events.note: Creates a human-touch task — a finished robot must hand back to a person.

events.name: automation.executed
events.note: This is the answer to 'why did the system text my lead?'. Without it, automation becomes a black box sellers distrust and disable. Note what is NOT here: automation.action_requested was deleted so automations call the owning module's command path instead of writing through a parallel path that bypasses every gate.

events.name: earnings.updated
events.note: Append-only SIGNED deltas with a period_key on every row. Never store a mutable total as the source of truth. delta is signed: a reversal is a negative append, not an edit — the ledger is forward-only and there is no recompute job.

events.name: leaderboard.rank_changed
events.note: Carries names, avatars, totals and ranks ONLY — never lead data. This is how performance stays public while books of business stay private, and it is the one legitimate cross-silo broadcast.

events.name: celebration.triggered
events.note: Fired AFTER the undo window (undo_deadline, 5000 ms) — never at the moment of the drag. amount display is a supervisor policy toggle; some floors celebrate the win, not the number.

events.name: pipeline.stage_config_changed
events.note: The nastiest hidden dependency in the system: a per-seller stage tweak can silently move a PUBLIC leaderboard. Almost every module spec forgets this event exists. Automations with stage-bound rules may now point at a deleted stage — must be flagged, not silently broken.

events.name: admin.setting_changed
events.note: Deliberately generic ONLY for low-blast-radius settings. Anything that can move money — stage closed flags — gets its own explicit event. Routed to the owning module by setting_key.

events.name: user.deactivated
events.note: An all-time leaderboard with no departure policy eventually shows a #1 who left two years ago. earnings_disposition forces the decision at the moment it matters.

events.name: lead.reposted
events.note: A vendor re-posts a lead the same seller already owns; the record updates in place instead of creating a second card. Without it the re-post is invisible: no timeline entry, and the vendor's duplicate rate cannot be measured.

events.name: compliance.send_blocked
events.note: THE NUMBER THAT PROVES THE GATE WORKS. Without it we can count sends and failures but never REFUSALS. The plain-English reason is written to the timeline, so `reason` must stay a stable code that the microcopy maps from.

events.name: compliance.override_started
events.note: Break-glass. Legally load-bearing: who opened the door, and when.

events.name: compliance.override_ended
events.note: Duration is what an auditor asks for. sends_permitted_count answers the second question they ask.

events.name: appointment.starting_soon
events.note: T-15m. The notification trigger both the flows and the stories assumed existed. Distinct from the T-1h SMS reminder, which is a message.sent with related_appointment_id.

events.name: opportunity.gate_blocked
events.note: Proves the win/loss guard is FIRING rather than being bypassed. Binds to stage_type, never to a stage name — renaming a column must change nothing.

events.name: contact.owner_changed
events.note: Ownership moves leads AND money between books; it cannot be silent. Admin-only and single-record by design — this is the exact seam where a routing engine would get smuggled in against the silo rule.

events.name: contact.bad_number_flagged
events.note: Drives dial suppression and vendor data-quality reporting. A number marked bad must stop being offered by every surface that dials, or the seller keeps burning attempts on a line that cannot connect.

events.name: integration.mapping_verified
events.note: THE ROLLOUT GUARD: an unverified map silently routes leads into the wrong book. This is item 1 of the first-run checklist, which cannot complete until this event can be emitted.

$note: Names that were RULED OUT, with the remap target and the consequence of
using them. §2 calls these the real finding — each one is a silent
integration failure, so the gate reports the consequence and not just
therefore NOT one of the 49 and is itself a ghost — an intermediate ruling
that reads like a decision if you stop at §2.

names.consequence: Six modules were waiting for this name. Celebration, task-closing and reporting never fire on a sale — and nothing goes red.
The 7-day cold rule has no home; board badges never appear. Cold is a property of the opportunity, not of the lead.
Sequences never auto-pause on reply — robots keep texting people who already answered.
Same as email.received. The channel is an enum on one event, which is also how WhatsApp arrives later without touching a consumer.
A STOP is honored on SMS but NOT on the dialer. One canonical consent event is what makes a revocation reach every channel.
Booked meetings never reach My Day or the card.
Booked meetings never reach My Day or the card. Note the spelling: the catalog is en-US with one L.
Two activity models. My Day becomes a lie because half the work is in the other one.
Two activity models, and the staleness clock reads the wrong one — so the cold rule fires on leads that were just worked.
Two activity models; overdue escalation silently covers half the work.
Cold threshold changes are silently ignored.
Stage-flag changes are silently ignored — which means a closed_won toggle moves a PUBLIC leaderboard with no recompute.

DELETED, not remapped. Four modules expected it. Automations call the owning module's command path instead; a dedicated action event is a parallel write path that bypasses every gate — including the one compliance gate.
Routing sneaking in the back door. Ownership is bound deterministically at the source; there is no routing engine.
§2's intermediate remap target, superseded by §4b. Reading §2 alone and stopping there produces this name.
Derived, not an event. First-touch latency is a field on the opportunity computed from call.completed. An event here would be a second source of truth for a number the board already shows.
Redundant. earnings.updated carries a SIGNED delta plus the triggering event; three names for one fact re-creates the drift this catalog exists to prevent.
Redundant — a reversal is a negative delta on the one event. A separate name invites a mutable total.
Redundant — an admin adjustment is a signed delta with its own triggering_event_name.
No consumer in the MVP. The notification-fatigue metric it would feed is out of scope.
Rejected: surveillance with no operational payoff.
A projection, not an event. last_activity_at is derived; a second writer is how it stops matching the timeline.
Derived. It is a state on the thread, not an event.
Remapped — the outcome is carried by appointment.completed or appointment.no_showed, which is what makes held-rate reporting possible.
Stage-flag changes silently ignored, including the closed_won toggle that moves money.
The import is a job with a result, not a per-row fact. Per-row emission would flood every consumer.
Three Aloware webhooks collapse into one internal event with parts_available[]. Three names means three handlers and three chances to duplicate the timeline row.
Same collapse — parts_available[] carries which half arrived.
Same collapse — the AloAi summary is a part, not an event.
Channel is an enum on one event. A per-channel event family is what makes WhatsApp a rewrite instead of a new enum member.
Channel is an enum on one event. Email itself is deferred to V1.1; the slot is already here.
A reminder IS a message — message.sent with related_appointment_id. A separate event would let a reminder skip the one compliance gate that every message passes.
The board is not an event source. A card is a rendering of an opportunity; emitting from the UI is how a move made by API never reaches a consumer.
